findings.summary: A6 / M4: the same-source-read invariant is not actually verified. The fetch stub returns an identical headOpen() (message_id "msg_001") for every /entities/ request and the test never constrains how many entity reads occur, so an implementation that performs a second independent getEntity and supersedes on that later head passes this assertion unchanged. Mutation M4 ("supersedes comes from a second independent read") survives the delivered suite. This is the mutual-exclusion invariant that is the stated reason the package exists (spec §2 D4, §4 A6, §6 M4), and it is left structurally unfalsifiable — the same zero-power pattern D4 was raised to eliminate. Killing M4 requires the entity stub to return a different message_id on the second read (or an explicit assertion that exactly one entity read was issued).

A1 / M1: no assertion discriminates numeric-status classification from substring matching. This case is named "error classification relies on numeric status, not message text" but stubs a genuine HTTP 409 whose body also contains "409", so it passes identically under the reverted msg.includes("409") implementation. The other classification cases (cas.test.ts:125-149) use HTTP 409/422 with default empty bodies and are likewise indifferent. The actual D1 defect — a non-409 failure whose response body happens to contain "409" must NOT be classified as conflict — is never exercised anywhere in the suite, so mutation M1 survives. Note that src/bus.ts:196-205 is itself correct and A1's mechanical grep check passes; the gap is that spec §6 makes M1→A2/A1 attribution normative and the test named for it has no power over it.

The delivered runner for the gate smoke obligation cannot execute: the smoke:cas script invokes tsx, but tsx appears neither in devDependencies (package.json:12-15) nor anywhere in package-lock.json, so after the mandated npm ci the command fails with "tsx: not found". Spec §3 permits only new script entries in package.json, so the dependency cannot be added under this delivery scope; a runner that works with the frozen dependency set (e.g. the Node type-stripping loader or the already-present vitest/tsc toolchain) is required for the §5 gate obligation to be dischargeable.

Smoke step ③ weakens the assertion the spec prescribes. Spec §5 requires asserting error === "conflict" on the second claim; the script only asserts !second.success, so a re-claim that failed with entity_not_found or invalid_payload would be reported as a passing smoke run — the same failure-classification blindness D1/D2 exist to remove.

Idempotency keys are derived from Date.now(), so every invocation produces fresh keys and an accidental re-run appends new messages instead of being deduplicated bus-side. Against an append-only channel with no DELETE route (spec §5), a fixed deterministic key per step would make a repeat run write zero new messages and is the only mechanical guard behind the prose "do not run repeatedly" instruction.

Verified as satisfied and not in dispute: D1 numeric classification with err.status on the thrown error (src/bus.ts:33-42, 196-205, zero includes("4xx") hits in src/bus.ts); D2 getEntity returning null only on 404 and rethrowing otherwise, with claimClue propagating read failures rather than degrading to entity_not_found (src/bus.ts:90-100, 224-227); D3 afterSeq !== undefined so afterSeq=0 reaches the query string (src/bus.ts:81); A5 test/cas.test.ts imports the real ../src/bus exports with no local casClaim copy; A7 test/protocol.test.ts still carries its original 11 cases; src/protocol.ts is untouched. The Continuous review committed in the RC subject recorded APPROVE with zero findings; this Final judgment is independent of it and does not adopt it.
